title: Mutations
examples: What is the difference between a gene mutation and a chromosomal mutation?
Can a mutation be harmful to an organism?
How does a mutation change the resulting protein?

explain.say: A mutation is a change in the genetic material.
Gene mutations change the sequence of one or a few bases.
Chromosomal mutations involve changes to the structure of whole chromosomes.
A deletion removes a piece of a chromosome entirely.
The effect of a mutation depends on where it occurs.
In everyday life, sickle cell anaemia is caused by a gene mutation.

items: Sickle Cell Anaemia | Gene mutation in haemoglobin gene

faq.q: What is the difference between a gene mutation and a chromosomal mutation?
faq.a: Gene mutations are changes in the DNA base sequence of a single gene. Chromosomal mutations are much larger changes affecting large parts of the chromosome structure.
asks: Are these two types of mutations related?
What scale of change do they represent?

faq.q: Can a mutation sometimes be beneficial to an organism?
faq.a: Yes, some mutations can provide an advantage that helps an organism survive in a new environment. This is key to evolution.
asks: How can a mutation help survival?

faq.q: If a mutation changes the protein, does it always stop working?
faq.a: Not always. Sometimes the change in one amino acid has no effect on the protein's function. This is called a silent mutation.
asks: Does every change break the protein?

faq.q: Where in the body are mutations most likely to occur?
faq.a: Mutations can occur in any cell, but those in germline cells can be passed down to offspring. This is important for heredity.
asks: Can I pass on a mutation?
Which cells are most critical for mutation study?

faq.q: What is the term for the study of mutations?
faq.a: The study of mutations is called mutation genetics. It helps us understand how genetic variation arises.
asks: What is the science of mutations?

facts: Gene mutations alter the nucleotide sequence within a gene.
Chromosomal mutations involve changes in chromosome number or structure.
A missense mutation changes one amino acid in the protein.
The effect of a mutation can be neutral, harmful, or beneficial.

quiz.say: A change in the DNA base sequence of a single gene is called a:
quiz.why: Gene mutations affect the code within a specific gene, changing the sequence of bases.

wrong.0: This is wrong because protein folding is the process the protein undergoes, not the change in the DNA itself.
wrong.2: This is wrong because chromosomal mutations involve large pieces of chromosomes, not just a few bases.
wrong.3: This is wrong because an allele shift describes a change in gene frequency in a population, not the physical change in the DNA.

quiz.say: If a mutation causes a stop codon prematurely, what is the likely effect on the protein?
quiz.why: A premature stop codon usually results in a severely shortened and non-functional protein.

wrong.0: This is wrong because losing part of the sequence usually weakens the protein structure.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the protein is cut short, meaning it cannot perform its intended job.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the ribosome reads the stop codon and stops translation immediately.

quiz.say: Which type of mutation involves the loss of a large segment of a chromosome?
quiz.why: Deletion specifically means that a piece of the chromosome has been lost or removed entirely.

wrong.0: This is wrong because translocation involves moving a segment to a different location, not losing it.
wrong.1: This is wrong because point mutations are small changes in the base sequence, not large chromosome segments.
wrong.3: This is wrong because duplication means a segment is copied and present twice, not lost.
